transcript.text: new washer jumpin all over the kitchen on spin like its gonna take off?? only had it 2 days

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. That sounds alarming, but on a machine only two days old it is almost certainly an installation issue rather than a broken part. The most likely cause is that the transit bolts (shipping screws) used to lock the drum for delivery were not removed from the back of the machine; these prevent the suspension from working and will make the unit jump violently. Please check the rear panel for 3 or 4 large bolts with plastic spacers. If they are still in, remove them immediately and try a spin cycle again. If they have already been removed, please let me know so we can check if the machine is level on the floor.
[Helpful to see: image "Check the transit bolts have been removed" — Transit bolts hold the drum still for delivery and must be removed before use — a machine that bangs, walks or vibrates (especially when new or recently moved) often still has them fitted. They unscrew from the back of the machine. Typical layout — your machine may differ.]
ok unplugged it. theres 3 big bolts with plastic bits still in the back and a hole with a plastic cap in it?? is that them? no water leaking btw

[Heading: Transit bolts still fitted]
Yes, those are definitely the transit bolts. They lock the drum for shipping and must be removed before use; leaving them in will cause exactly that violent jumping. Please unscrew and remove all three (and any fourth one if present) using a spanner or socket. Keep the plastic spacers and washers you find inside, as you'll need them if you ever move the machine again. Once they are out, plug the machine back in and run a spin cycle to confirm it is stable.
ok found a spanner and some plastic caps in the bag that was in the drum, will try that. is the hole with the cap ok to leave?

[Heading: Transit bolts]
Yes, that empty hole is normal; just push the plastic cap back in to keep dust out. Once you've removed all three bolts and re-tested a spin cycle with no laundry inside, please let me know if it runs smoothly or if it still jumps.
ok took all 3 bolts out and ran a rinse and spin. much quieter now, bit of vibration but it stays put

[Heading: Transit bolts removed; vibration likely due to levelling or load balance.]
That is excellent news. The violent jumping was definitely caused by the transit bolts being left in place. Since it now stays put but still vibrates a bit, this is normal for a new machine until you get used to its specific behaviour or adjust it slightly. 1. Ensure the machine is perfectly level (use a spirit level if you have one) and that all four feet are firmly touching the floor with their lock nuts tightened against the base.
2. Avoid washing single heavy items like duvets or bath mats on high spins; these often cause imbalance. Distribute laundry evenly.
3. If it vibrates heavily again, pause the cycle and redistribute the load manually before restarting. If the vibration becomes violent again or the machine starts walking across the floor despite being level, please let me know.

candidates.cause: Machine not level or feet loose
